meta.what: Numbers the authors publish about their own work, quoted from the page we read them on. None of these are our measurements — ours are on /typesafe-jev/statistics, and they are labelled as ours.
meta.shape: value / label / quote / from / source. The label says what the number is about, and it says so even when the answer is unflattering to the entry: a number about a local substitute model, an OCR pass or a whole run is not a Jev decision and does not pretend to be one.
meta.cameFrom: The reference site (madewithjev.com) prints one of these on every card as a bare figure with the label in a tooltip. Copied as a function — a card that shows a number is more useful than one that only describes — and hardened in the one place we differ from it: our label is visible text, and the sentence the number came from is attached.

gh:browser-use/jev-ultrafast.label: one flight search, start to finish
gh:browser-use/jev-ultrafast.quote: Zürich → London on Google Flights in 7.1 seconds. One natural-language goal, actual text generation, and loading waits included.

gh:jarrodwatts/jev-trader.label: the budget for one buy or sell decision
gh:jarrodwatts/jev-trader.quote: A TypeSafe Jev model watches the Kuru MON-USDC order book and answers buy or sell every ~300 ms.

gh:jarrodwatts/jev-trader.label: one RPC read of the order book, on the public endpoint
gh:jarrodwatts/jev-trader.quote: the hot loop makes exactly two RPC round trips: one eth_call for the book (~18 ms on the public RPC, READ_RPC_URL) and one eth_sendRawTransaction

gh:reticlehq/reticle.label: checking a 2.6-second time-gated transition instead of waiting it out
gh:reticlehq/reticle.quote: Wall-clock time to a verdict: a 2.6 second time-gated transition verified in 176 ms versus a 2,978 ms real wait, and a 16-flow batch in 5.2 seconds versus 31.7 seconds one at a time.

gh:awlevin/typesafe-computer-use.label: one full step at p50, of which ~280–350 ms is the decision
gh:awlevin/typesafe-computer-use.quote: End-to-end loop, p50: 302-380 ms per step (2.6-3.5 steps/sec), of which ~280-350 ms is the TypeSafe decision.
